images.caption: Figure 1:Observation and execution control in computer-use agents.(a) Fixed scheduling.Reasoning continues after a dialog appears, and fixed waits continue after the page is ready.(b) Passive watching.Buffered frames inform later observations, while pre-dispatch checks can reject actions after reasoning completes.(c) Proactive perception.NightWatchcombines a0.8B System-1 watcherwith threshold rules to interrupt reasoning, void pending actions, and end post-action waits based on estimated interface state.(d) OSWorld-Verified results.NightWatchreduces non-reasoning time by 33% and the wasted-time share from 16.3% to 7.7% at comparable success with the same agent.

Figure 5:One intervention of each kindfrom the runs ofTable1with MiMo-V2.6-Flash. Top: the screenshot the agent reasons on; bottom: the screen whenNightWatchintervenes. Interrupt: a second server turns red while the agent is reasoning about the first. Void: the swatches rotate before the click on the cyan one is dispatched (red circle: click point), so the click is discarded. Wake: a terminal command returns, and the agent observes the result 1.1 s later.
